title: Edge demultiplexing transformer: normalize structured logs and route to Loki/ELK
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Several services emit wide-variety JSON logs and binary blobs at the edge. Downstream aggregation into Loki/ELK is inconsistent: fields are duplicated, tenant and trace correlation is lost in high-cardinality cases, and payload sizes spike due to redundant metadata. This ticket is to design and implement an edge-side demultiplexing transformer (a lightweight sidecar/proxy) that normalizes structured logs, strips/flags PII, preserves correlation IDs (trace_id, span_id, request_id), and routes compacted records to the appropriate Loki/ELK tenant stream or to NDJSON blob storage for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end preservation of correlation ids: trace_id and request_id present in 99.9% of logs emitted after transformer when input contained them
Normalized JSON schema applied to >= 90% of incoming structured events (schema mapping fallback to 'raw' when unknown)
Observed per-request p50 latency overhead from sidecar <= 5ms on typical 100-200 byte log payloads at 5k RPS per instance
Average per-event payload size reduction >= 30% for noisy headers/metadata heavy events
Configurable tenant routing header respected; events routed to Loki with correct tenant label or to ELK pipeline when configured
PII redaction module can be toggled per-tenant and redact fields according to policy table without deploy
Integration tests cover schema-permutation cases and confirm trace_id stitching in Grafana latency dashboards
Graceful degradation: when Loki is unavailable, buffered events are written to durable blob (S3) and an alert is emitted; no loss of trace linkage
Operational metrics emitted: transform_latency_ms (p50/p95), dropped_events_count, routing_failures_count, buffer_backpressure_active (bool)
Security review completed and KMS keys referenced for any persisted blobs containing sensitive headers
tasks: Design sketch + API contract for transformer (schema mapping DSL, redact rules, tenant routing headers)
Prototype Rust sidecar binary with hyper/reqwest for low-overhead JSON streaming
Implement schema-mapper with small default built-in mappings and extension hooks
Add PII-redaction plugin with safe-sanitizers and allow per-tenant rule set via remote config
Integrate Loki client with batched push endpoint and tenant header handling
Add fallback S3 blob writer with encrypted objects and retention tagging
Benchmarks and perf tests (latency, throughput, CPU/memory) at 1k/5k/20k RPS
Unit + integration tests with local Loki/ELK test harness and trace propagation assertions
Run canary on staging edge fleet and capture dashboards for 72h before gradual rollout
Documentation for SDK integration, config flags, and runbook for buffer/backpressure scenarios
decision_log: 2025-03-13: Chosen edge-sidecar model over centralized ingest lambda due to <5ms p50 latency target and tenant-aware routing needs
2025-03-14: Selected Rust for prototype because of low allocation overhead and existing RedProc crate we can reuse
2025-03-16: Decided on CDC-style schema mapping DSL (yaml) with deterministic field transform order vs. on-the-fly JS transforms to reduce runtime overhead
2025-03-18: Buffering strategy: bounded ring buffer per-tenant with backpressure signal to producers; on full => drop non-critical fields before full-drop
2025-03-19: Persist fallback chosen as encrypted S3 objects (lifecycle 90 days) and a matching 'debug-id' written to primary logs for lookup
notes: Initial spike showed naive JSON reserializing added ~12MB/s CPU overhead at 10k RPS; micro-optimizations (zero-copy parsing, field projection) are required

Tradeoffs: strict schema normalization will simplify downstream analytics but will increase mismatch cases for legacy producers — mitigated via 'raw' passthrough bucket and producer onboarding checklist
Monitoring plan: add Loki-side synthetic trace joiner job to validate correlation stitching nightly
Potential future: expose small SDK (go/node) that emits pre-normalized logs to bypass sidecar for high-throughput services
Team notes: coordinate rollout with platform on-call and SEs for tenants with regulatory requirements (EU PII rules)
